03. This matter is taken up through hybrid mode.
2. This application has been filed for condonation of delay of 208 days in presenting the Memorandum of Appeal.
3. Learned Counsel for the private Respondents files objection to the application in Court.
The same is taken on record.
4. In view of the reasons assigned in this application so also submission made by the learned Counsel for the Appellant-Union of India, the delay is condoned.
5. Accordingly, the I.A. stands disposed of.
(S. K. Mishra) Judge PTO 04. 1.

Though the matter is listed under the heading "For Orders" for consideration of the application for condonation of delay, as the delay has already been condoned vide order of date passed in I.A. No.192 of 2024, the Appeal is taken up for hearing and disposed of at the stage of admission, on consent of learned Counsel for the parties.

2. This Appeal has been preferred challenging the judgment dated 30th June, 2023 passed in L.A.
Case No.415 of 2014 (CIS No.28-2015) by the Senior Civil Judge, Balasore, vide which compensation has been enhanced from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.48,000/- per decimal.

It is not disputed at the Bar that the notification for acquisition of the suit land pertains to the Notification as of the suit land, which Union Of India vs Biswanath Das (Dead) on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151825747/
1 was the subject matter in L.A.A. No.89 of 2018.

entities.text: Union Of India vs Biswanath Das (Dead) on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It further reveals from the impugned judgment that the referral Court, relying on the Judgment of this Court passed in L.A.A. No.89 of 2018, which was marked Ext.2 on admission, enhanced the compensation and ordered for payment of the same for acquisition of the land of the private Respondents along with additional market value @ 12% per annum from the date of publication of notice U/s. 4(1) of the L.A. Act, 1894.

Apart from that, it has also been directed to pay statutory solatium @ 30% on the market value and interest @ 9% per annum for the 1st year after acquisition and @ 15% for the subsequent year till the date of the said order within a period of four months.
Hence, this Court is not inclined to entertain the prayer made in the Appeal.
3. Accordingly, the Appeal stands dismissed.

4. In view of the dismissal of the Appeal, the Appellant- Union of India is directed to implement the impugned Judgment dated 30th June, 2023 passed in L.A. Case No.415 of 2014 (CIS No.28-2015)
within a period of four months hence.
5. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted on proper application as per rules.

Prasant (S. K. Mishra)
 Judge  Signed by: PRASANT KUMAR PRADHAN
